title: Pious doubters still belong among the faithful — do not drive them to despair
source_text: CI. Adde quod testatur experientia multos homines pios atque Dei timentes, quiique nullo modo dubitant de veritate Verbi Dei, & promissionum in eo contentarum, ac jugiter & serio ad Deum confugiunt, & ejus gratiam ac misericordiam ardentibus precibus implorant, nondum tamen esse certos de illa impetrata, quoniam scrupulis variis vexati anxii sunt de propria sua dispositione, & de propria fide & poenitentia dubitant, an satis seria atque syncera sit. Quos certe nulla ratio est, cur e vere fidelium numero excludamus. Nec videtur quomodo possimus conscientias eorum afflictas solari atque erigere, nisi doceamus eos hanc fidem per quam ad Deum confugiunt, & gratiam ejus sitiunt, & implorant, esse illam ipsam cui Deus peccatorum remissionem & salutem promisit. Imo vero viam ad desperationem sterneret, qui simpliciter eos hortaretur, ut certi sint de Dei gratia, quasi sine hoc vera fides esse nequiret.
pass_a_gloss: Add that experience testifies that many pious men and God-fearers, who in no way doubt the truth of the Word of God and of the promises contained in it, and continually and seriously flee to God, and with ardent prayers implore his grace and mercy, are nevertheless not yet certain of that obtained, because vexed with various scruples they are anxious about their own disposition, and doubt concerning their own faith and repentance, whether it is serious and sincere enough. Whom certainly there is no reason why we should exclude from the number of the truly faithful. Nor does it seem how we can console and raise their afflicted consciences unless we teach them that this faith by which they flee to God, and thirst for and implore his grace, is that very faith to which God has promised remission of sins and salvation. Nay rather, he would lay a path to desperation who should simply exhort them to be certain of God's grace, as if without this true faith could not be.
pass_b_english: Experience: many godly people trust God’s Word and promises, flee to him, and plead for mercy — yet are not sure grace is already theirs, anxious about whether their faith and repentance are sincere enough.
No reason to cast them out of the truly faithful.
Console them: the faith by which they flee and thirst is itself the faith to which God promised remission and salvation.
To demand certainty of obtained grace as if without it there is no true faith is to pave the way to despair.
